document.title: Learning Models for Pressure Forecasting
document.research_task: Supervised regression for 15-minute-ahead pressure forecasting at sensor n1

main_objective: Implement targeted improvements while preserving the technical accuracy, original research, experimental design, figures, numerical results, and professional presentation of the existing document.

priority_improvements.location: Page 3, Section 2: Contributions of Previous Authors
instructions: Add a concise paragraph following the comparative literature table.
Clearly distinguish pressure forecasting from leak detection, leak localization, and current-pressure reconstruction.
Explain why the reviewed studies do not provide a directly comparable evaluation of 15-minute-ahead pressure forecasting at sensor n1 using the released BattLeDIM SCADA data.
Connect the identified gap directly to the proposed Gradient Boosting experiment.
Use qualified language such as 'Among the reviewed studies' rather than claiming worldwide novelty.
Explain the scientific value of comparing classical regression models with more complex approaches under a consistent evaluation protocol.
priority_improvements.suggested_text: Among the reviewed studies, none reports a directly comparable evaluation of 15-minute-ahead pressure forecasting at sensor n1 using the released BattLeDIM SCADA measurements. Existing approaches primarily address leak diagnosis, current-pressure estimation, or forecasting under different simulated conditions and prediction horizons. This motivates a controlled comparison of conventional regression models using a common temporal evaluation protocol and physically motivated hydraulic features. The proposed experiment evaluates whether Gradient Boosting improves upon persistence, Ridge Regression, and Random Forest, and whether auxiliary measurements provide predictive value beyond the target sensor's own history.
